svg.title: From cosmic rays to what RadiaCode records in flight
svg.desc: A left-to-right scientific schematic showing a primary cosmic ray creating representative nucleon, electromagnetic, and muonic branches connected only by named collision, pion-decay, and photon-conversion events. One representative muon path continues through aircraft altitude to the ground. A ground-level callout notes that muons dominate the penetrating charged cosmic-ray component while neutrons, photons, electrons, positrons, and some protons also remain. The right side shows local aircraft geometry, the 10 millimeter CsI(Tl) cube, its gamma-calibrated visible-energy response, and recorded detector observables. A prominent boundary states that pulse height does not identify particle species or directly measure primary cosmic-ray flux.
svg.text: From cosmic rays to what RadiaCode records in flight
The atmosphere creates a mixed secondary field; RadiaCode records pulse height reported as γ-calibrated visible energy.

RadiaCode records pulse height as γ-calibrated visible energy — not particle identity, direction, or primary cosmic-ray flux.
Incident energy, particle fluence, or dose require a validated response + geometry model; the terminal bin is a catch-all channel.
